prop:sl-n-color-framing:
Proposition The \mathrm{SU}(N) framing reproduces the one-gluon color factors. Let V be the vector representation of \mathrm{U}_q(\mathfrak{gl}_N) and let \sigma_i act on V^{\otimes n} by the Jimbo braiding [jimbo1986], with eigenvalue q on \mathrm{Sym}^2 V and -q^{-1} on \Lambda^2 V. Put \sigma_i^{\mathfrak{sl}} := q^{-1/N}\,\sigma_i. Then:

  1. the eigenvalues of \sigma_i^{\mathfrak{sl}} on \mathrm{Sym}^2 V and \Lambda^2 V are q^{2 c_{\mathrm{S}}} and -q^{2 c_{\mathrm{A}}}, where c_R := \tfrac12\bigl(C_2(R) - 2C_F\bigr) is the one-gluon color factor, c_{\mathrm{S}} = \tfrac{N-1}{2N} and c_{\mathrm{A}} = -\tfrac{N+1}{2N};
  2. the eigenvalues of \sigma_i itself are q^{2c_R + 1/N} up to sign;
  3. the ratio c_{\mathrm{A}}/c_{\mathrm{S}} = -\tfrac{N+1}{N-1} equals -2 if and only if N = 3;
  4. q^{-1/N} is the unique positive scalar c for which the monodromy of V around \Lambda^N V under c\,\sigma_i is the identity.

Proof. Items 1--3 are identities in \mathbb{Q}(N). They use the Casimir values C_F = \tfrac{N^2-1}{2N}, C_2(\mathrm{Sym}^2 V) = \tfrac{(N-1)(N+2)}{N} and C_2(\Lambda^2 V) = \tfrac{(N+1)(N-2)}{N}, together with the ribbon formula for the braiding on a summand of V \otimes V [kassel1995].

For item 4, the full twist acts on the irreducible summand indexed by \lambda as q^{2\,\mathrm{ct}(\lambda)}, where \mathrm{ct}(\lambda) is the sum of contents. The tensor product V \otimes \Lambda^N V is the summand \lambda = (2, 1^{N-1}), and \Lambda^N V is (1^N). So the monodromy of V around \Lambda^N V is q^{2\,\mathrm{ct}(2,1^{N-1}) - 2\,\mathrm{ct}(1^N)} = q^{2}. The braid has 2N crossings, so rescaling to c\,\sigma_i multiplies the monodromy by c^{2N}. The condition c^{2N} q^2 = 1 with c > 0 forces c = q^{-1/N}. \square

The value q^2 of the monodromy is computed on explicit Jimbo matrices for N = 2, 3 and from contents for all N.
rem:sl-n-color-frame-scope:
Remark Scope of the \mathrm{SU}(N) frame. Convention. A color observable is read with the framed generator \sigma_i^{\mathfrak{sl}} = q^{-1/N}\sigma_i of Proposition. Every other observable keeps the Hecke normalisation (\sigma_i - q)(\sigma_i + q^{-1}) = 0. The rescaling is not applied to the Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1) or to the writhe-normalised Markov trace. A uniform rescaling would multiply an unnormalised trace \mathrm{tr}_M(w) by q^{-\mathrm{wr}(w)/N}, where \mathrm{wr}(w) is the writhe of the word w, and would send z to q^{-1/N} z. Words of writhe zero are unaffected; words of nonzero writhe are not, so the scope matters.

The two-strand color factors. In the Hecke normalisation the two exchange channels of 3 \otimes 3 = \bar 3 \oplus 6 have log-exponents \pm 1. Their ratio is 1, against the group-theoretic |c_{\bar 3}/c_6| = 2. In the \mathrm{SU}(3) frame the log-exponents are -\tfrac43 and \tfrac23, so the ratio is 2 with both signs correct.

What the factor 2 was. The identity \log|\lambda_{\mathrm{S}}| + \log|\lambda_{\mathrm{A}}| = 0 for the Hecke eigenvalues, i.e. |\det \sigma_i| = 1 on V \otimes V, is the statement that the \mathfrak{u}_1 summand of \mathfrak{gl}_N = \mathfrak{sl}_N \oplus \mathfrak{u}_1 shifts both exponents by the same 1/N. It is a normalisation of the generator, not a structural obstruction to the color sector.

The nuclear channel is not repaired. The same frame at N = 2 gives the channel ratio (N+1)/(N-1) = 3. The nuclear T = 0 / T = 1 ratio it would have to reproduce is \approx 33.7. So the color frame does not supply the missing nuclear mechanism. This is a scope-limited negative: it says that this frame alone does not reach 33.7, not that framing cannot enter a nuclear closure.

rem:torus-knot-flavour-labels-prior-art:
Remark Prior art: q-integer differences are Alexander polynomials of (2n-1,2) torus knots. With symmetric q-integers [n]_q = (q^n - q^{-n})/(q - q^{-1}), Gavrilik observes that the differences [n]_q - [n-1]_q are the Alexander polynomials of the (2n-1,2) torus knots [gavrilik2001, \S 2, p. 2]:

[2]_q - 1 = \Delta_q\{3_1\},\qquad [3]_q - [2]_q = \Delta_q\{5_1\},\qquad [4]_q - [3]_q = \Delta_q\{7_1\}.

In the same section the torus knots 5_1, 7_1, 9_1, 11_1 are put in correspondence with the vector quarkonia s\bar s, c\bar c, b\bar b, t\bar t, as part of U_q(\mathfrak{su}_n) mass sum rules.

The identity is parameter-free and uses the same q-integers as the corpus. The assignment of the T(2,2k+1) family is a different matter: the flavour layer of the dictionary assigns it to leptons, and the trefoil–cinquefoil channel uses T(2,3) and T(2,5) for the colour tube, while Gavrilik assigns it to quarkonia. These are three different readings of one knot family. The paper takes q at a root of [n]_q - [n-1]_q, a root of unity such as e^{i\pi/5}, and compares the resulting mass relations with data at the per-cent level. It works on the unit circle, not at the real q_0, so it supplies the identity but no support for any one assignment.

The chapter cannot do without N = 3: the meson octet, the baryon multiplets, and every quark row of the dictionary are conditional on a three-dimensional partner, which is unavailable from a single fibre. As shown in the Standard Model appendix and in the flavour-charges remark, hypercharge is coupled to that same missing partner: on the split bundle F = V_2 \oplus W_3^* (z_3 = q^3/[3]_q), tracelessness forces y_3 = -\tfrac{2}{3}y_2 with no free parameter, whereas without W_3^* the chapter reproduces I_3 alone and cannot close the Gell-Mann--Nishijima relation.

  1. The N = 3 problem. Schur--Weyl duality [jimbo1986] (Proposition) requires the fundamental representation to be 3-dimensional. The single-fibre tower has \dim V = 2 (the standard single-fibre construction; the Descartes condition \chi(\mathcal{A}) = -6 is compatible with but does not uniquely force N = 2). That N = 2 cannot host the decomposition is now proved (the alternating channel \binom{N}{3} vanishes iff N < 3, and the decuplet dimension forces N = 3) --- so the obstruction is settled and only the construction is missing. Open: construct a three-dimensional object W in the multi-fibre groupoid whose symmetric square \mathrm{Sym}^2(W) is irreducible (no singlet). The octonion G_2 route supplies a colour \mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{c}} candidate that the gate does not exclude --- not excluded rather than passes, since the singlet count 0 that would make it pass is the cited \mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{c}}-irreducibility input and not a proved one (see the ledger). Whether it yields flavour \mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{f}} is untested.

    What such a construction must supply is now a theorem, and it is one property rather than a list. Putting the two halves together: a three-dimensional object passing the gate must contain a complex-type irrep , and a category all of whose irreps are self-dual contains none — which is precisely the single-fibre case, since every \mathrm{SU}(2) irrep is self-dual. So the property a groupoid construction must exhibit is exactly the property one fibre lacks: non-self-duality. This yields a screening test : a candidate whose three-dimensional object is isomorphic to its own dual is dead, and can be discarded before its \mathrm{Sym}^2 decomposition is computed. It does not construct anything — Route A stays open — but it replaces "more structure" with a single checkable condition.

    The same condition is reachable from the row cap, independently. The Descartes characteristic \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(M_0) = -6 forces \mathrm{SU}(2), hence \dim V = 2, hence partitions of at most two rows, so the (1^3) block drops at n = 3 and a three-dimensional object cannot be a tensor power of the single fibre. That argument reaches non-self-duality without the \mathrm{Sym}^2 gate and without the Frobenius--Schur trichotomy, as the gate-and-trichotomy argument reaches it without the Euler characteristic and without Schur--Weyl. A third route reaches the same negative from a different direction again: N \neq 3 follows from non-degeneracy of the fibre's volume form (\Lambda^2 V \cong \mathbf{1} forces N = 2), without the \mathrm{Sym}^2 gate, the row cap or the Euler characteristic.

    The three are not three votes on one proposition, and the difference is what matters here. The row-cap and volume-form arguments bound the fibre: they say N = 2, so one fibre cannot supply a three-dimensional object. The gate-and-trichotomy argument bounds any candidate: it says which property a candidate must have, and so yields a test that can be applied to an object nobody has built yet. The negative is now over-determined; the screen is what is additive.

    That the search is confined to the groupoid level is now a theorem, not an extrapolation. The parity criterion decides the \mathrm{Sym}^2 gate for a single irreducible summand, and a three-dimensional W need not be irreducible --- W = V_{1/2} \oplus V_0 has dimension 3, sits in the tensor category generated by the fibre, and is not an irrep, so that criterion does not reach it. The multiplicity form closes the case: counting singlets by Frobenius--Schur type, a passing W must be a sum of pairwise distinct even-dimensional irreps, hence \dim W is even. Since 3 is odd, no three-dimensional object of the single-fibre category passes the gate, reducible or not. Any N = 3 must therefore come from genuinely multi-fibre structure --- which is what the route above asserts, now with a proved invariant behind it (a scope-(b) exclusion, the invariant being the Frobenius--Schur indicator (-1)^{2j}). Even dimension is necessary, not sufficient: V_{1/2}^{\oplus 2} has dimension 4 and fails the gate too, so the parity invariant prunes candidates rather than characterising them. The octonionic candidate is no counterexample to this: it is not an object of the single-fibre category at all, arising instead from G_2 = \mathrm{Aut}(\mathbb{O}), which is precisely why the parity exclusion leaves it standing.

    The mechanism behind that escape is now proved rather than asserted, and it is worth stating because it bounds how far the exclusion reaches. The parity argument runs through self-duality: every \mathrm{SU}(2) irrep satisfies V^* \cong V, so the cross terms V_i \otimes V_j contribute no singlet and the survivors are forced to be distinct even-dimensional irreps. A complex-type representation (\mathrm{FS} = 0, \mathbf{3} \not\cong \bar{\mathbf{3}}) pairs to a singlet only against its conjugate, so one whose conjugate is absent from the object passes the gate at any dimension, odd included --- and such an object is exhibited at dimension exactly 3. So the even-dimension exclusion above is a scope-(b) exclusion within the self-dual sector and is silent, not negative, outside it. This is the same non-self-duality that the colour construction already identifies as what the \mathrm{Sym}^2 gate consumes.

    Nor is the fibre functor the missing knob. The single-fibre category admits fibre functors of every dimension n \ge 2 [bichon2003]: for E \in \mathrm{GL}_n with \mathrm{tr}(E^{-1}E^{t}) = -q - q^{-1} the comodule category of the bilinear-form quantum group B(E) is monoidally equivalent to that of \mathcal{O}_q(\mathrm{SL}_2), and such E exist over \mathbb{R} at q_0 for every n \ge 3. So a three-dimensional image of V is available. It does not help, because a fibre functor is monoidal and therefore preserves the Clebsch--Gordan rule: under a three-dimensional fibre functor V^{\otimes 3} \cong V_{3/2} \oplus V_{1/2} \oplus V_{1/2} has dimensions 21 + 3 + 3, and under a fibre functor of any dimension the spin-0 summand the decomposition \mathbf{10} \oplus \mathbf{8} \oplus \mathbf{8} \oplus \mathbf{1} requires is absent from V^{\otimes 3} by parity . Dimension is a property of the fibre functor; the multiplet structure is a property of the category. This closes the single-fibre reading of Route A --- the question does the category admit inequivalent fibre functors? is answered affirmatively and turns out not to bear on N = 3 --- and relocates the missing object to the category itself: an object W with \Lambda^3 W \neq 0, which the categorical volume constraint (Definition, condition 5) forbids for the fundamental.

  2. Hypercharge Y. The writhe-to-isospin map w \mapsto I_3 is derived. The hypercharge Y is not: the writhe map is falsified as a Y assignment (proton and neutron share Y = +1 while their writhes differ). Open: identify a second crossing invariant independent of the writhe. Battery (exploratory, not wired): of 10{,}000 helon-style assignments, 4 survive --- but that ratio carries no corroboration, and is not a 2500\!:\!1 filter. It is proved that the spectrum battery is exactly T = 3Q (the -2I_3 common to candidate and target cancels, leaving the defining equation of Q_{\mathrm{twist}}, not a test of it); the nucleon check is entailed by charge additivity and states one condition twice; and the \mathbb{Z}_6 condition never sees the assignment, so it filters nothing. Each flavour is thus filtered independently by one linear equation, and 4 = 1 \times 2 \times 2 \times 1 counts multisets with totals 3Q = (2,-1,0,-3) --- the "uniquely determined" u and electron multisets being the two totals that admit a single multiset. A parameter-free repair using the canonical ribbon twist (Q = c(\lambda)/3, c the content sum) was tested and fails: at n = 3 it gives the integer charges \{+1,0,-1\}, and no n \le 8 yields both quark charges ; scope-(a) for that reading only. The derivation gap is therefore the entire content: whether the twist multisets are forced by the categorical braid words (not just consistent with them) is the open content of the hypercharge conjecture, and nothing else in the battery constrains anything. In the split-bundle framing F = V_2 \oplus W_3^* (z_3 = q^3/[3]_q) of the Standard Model appendix and the flavour-charges remark, tracelessness of \mathrm{diag}(y_2, y_2, y_3, y_3, y_3) forces y_3 = -\tfrac{2}{3}y_2, pinning the exterior-pair doublet hypercharge y_2 + y_3 = +\tfrac{1}{3} at y_2 = 1 with Killing Weinberg ratio 3/8, and separating \bar u (-\tfrac{2}{3}) from d (-\tfrac{1}{3}) despite their shared crossing sign -1. Hypercharge is thus reduced conditionally to the same missing object as item 1: constructing W_3 in the multi-fibre groupoid.

  3. Continuous G_2 completion. The discrete skeleton of \mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{c}} \subset G_2 = \mathrm{Aut}(\mathbb{O}) is verified (\mathrm{GL}(3, \mathbb{F}_2) \cong \mathrm{PSL}(2,7) Fano symmetry of the associator). The continuous Lie-group completion --- specifically the coset S^6 = G_2/\mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{c}} --- not constructed here: the continuous Lie group G_2 is not available. This is an infrastructure obstruction, not a structural one.

  4. Flavour versus colour separation. The octonionic \mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{c}} is colour. The eightfold-way classification requires flavour \mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{f}}. Whether these are the same, different, or related by a groupoid-level duality is open, and the \mathrm{Sym}^2 gate cannot settle it.

    In particular the gate does not show that the two cannot both come from the same construction. That it excludes the icosahedral triple T_1 while the G_2 route passes compares two different objects and establishes only that those two differ, not that one construction cannot supply both roles. (The T_1 comparison is in the Schur--Weyl proposition, where it is stated as not excluded on a literature decomposition.)

    The failure is structural, not a repairable gap in the inference. It is proved that at dimension three, passing the gate is equivalent to carrying a complex-type irrep. Any two three-dimensional objects that both pass are therefore both complex type, and the gate has returned the same verdict for each --- two distinct such objects are exhibited. A flavour triple and a colour triple that each pass are, to this gate, indistinguishable.

    What the gate does establish is a class exclusion: no real or quaternionic construction reaches dimension three through it, so T_1's failure is a consequence of its Frobenius--Schur type and not a fact about the icosahedron. Whatever separates flavour from colour lies elsewhere --- as it does for the \mathbb{Z}/3 grading, which is likewise shown to be blind to the identification.

    The two blindnesses are one blindness. prop:pairing-gauge-fluctuation-massless:
Proposition Pure-gauge fluctuations of a pairing are zero modes of the contraction action. Let \mathbf{C} be a monoidal category that is preadditive and R-linear over a commutative ring R, and let A^\vee, A be objects with an exact pairing A^\vee \dashv A (so that A is a right dual of A^\vee in the sense of a rigid monoidal category), with coevaluation \eta \colon \mathbf{1} \to A^\vee \otimes A. The field space of Frobenius pairings is the R-module \mathcal{P} = \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathbf{C}}(A^\vee \otimes A, \mathbf{1}). For a co-pairing \eta and a linear functional \varepsilon \colon \mathrm{End}(\mathbf{1}) \to R, the contraction action is the quadratic form

  S_{\eta,\varepsilon}(T) \;=\; \varepsilon(T \circ \eta)^2 ,
  \qquad
  \frac{\delta S_{\eta,\varepsilon}}{\delta T}(\delta) \;=\; 2\,\varepsilon(T\circ \eta)\,\varepsilon(\delta\circ\eta),

on \mathcal{P}, where the variational derivative is twice the symmetric bilinear form of S_{\eta,\varepsilon}; it satisfies the exact Taylor identity S(T+\delta) = S(T) + \frac{\delta S}{\delta T}(\delta) + S(\delta).

For f \in \mathrm{End}(A^\vee) with right adjoint mate f^{\vee} \in \mathrm{End}(A), the pure-gauge fluctuation of a background pairing \lambda \in \mathcal{P} is

  \delta_f \lambda \;=\; \lambda \circ \bigl( f \otimes \mathrm{id}_A \;-\; \mathrm{id}_{A^\vee} \otimes f^{\vee} \bigr).

For every f, every background \lambda and every field T \in \mathcal{P}:

  S_{\eta,\varepsilon}(\delta_f\lambda) = 0,
  \qquad
  \frac{\delta S_{\eta,\varepsilon}}{\delta T}(\delta_f\lambda) = 0,
  \qquad
  S_{\eta,\varepsilon}(T + \delta_f\lambda) = S_{\eta,\varepsilon}(T).

More generally, for any quadratic action S on an R-module, invariance under translation by a direction g holds if and only if S(g) = 0 and g lies in the radical of \delta S/\delta T for every T; such directions form a submodule. No hypothesis on 2 \in R is used.

The argument is one line: (f \otimes \mathrm{id}_A) \circ \eta = (\mathrm{id}_{A^\vee} \otimes f^{\vee}) \circ \eta is a standard property of the mate, so \delta_f\lambda \circ \eta = 0, and the contraction action sees \delta_f \lambda only through \delta_f\lambda \circ \eta.

The handedness of the Frobenius pairing. The exact pairing above has evaluation A \otimes A^\vee \to \mathbf{1}, which is not the Frobenius pairing A^\vee \otimes A \to \mathbf{1}. A non-degenerate Frobenius pairing instead makes A \dashv A^\vee exact, with the Frobenius pairing as evaluation and a coevaluation \tilde\eta \colon \mathbf{1} \to A \otimes A^\vee. If \mathbf{C} is a braided monoidal category, with braiding \beta, then \beta_{A,A^\vee} \circ \tilde\eta \colon \mathbf{1} \to A^\vee \otimes A is a co-pairing, and the same three conclusions hold for it, with the gauge fluctuation now \lambda \circ ( f \otimes \mathrm{id}_A - \mathrm{id}_{A^\vee} \otimes {}^{\vee}\! f), where {}^{\vee}\! f \in \mathrm{End}(A) is the left adjoint mate of f for A \dashv A^\vee. The argument is the same, with the mate identity transported through the naturality of \beta.

Scope. The contraction action has rank at most one, so its radical contains far more than the pure-gauge directions; the proposition says that gauge directions are among the zero modes, not that they exhaust them. Without a braiding, a non-degenerate Frobenius pairing supplies no co-pairing \mathbf{1} \to A^\vee \otimes A, and that case is not covered.

Under that reading, the proposition is the algebraic shadow of the familiar statement of linearised gravity that pure-gauge perturbations h \mapsto h + \mathcal{L}_\xi \bar g cost no action: the infinitesimal automorphism f plays the role of the vector field \xi, the combination f \otimes \mathrm{id} - \mathrm{id} \otimes f^{\vee} that of the Lie derivative of the background, and the vanishing of S(\delta_f\lambda) together with the radical condition is what "no mass term along gauge directions" means for a quadratic action.

def:mass-identity:
Definition Mass (Frobenius form of the mass integrand). Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe (quantum observable universe) and let \{A_n\}_{n \geq 0} be its recursive brane tower (recursive brane tower). Let \mu, \eta be the multiplication and unit of the Frobenius--Hopf object A, let \Delta \colon A \to A \otimes A be the comultiplication and let \int_A \colon A \to \mathbf{1} be the Frobenius form. The mass integrand is the endomorphism

  \Psi = (\textstyle\int_A \otimes \mathrm{id}) \circ \Delta \colon A \to A .

The inertial mass of a morphism \varrho \colon \mathbf{1} \to A (a "closed cycle" in the Frobenius--Hopf object) is the norm of the composite \mathbf{1} \xrightarrow{\varrho} A \xrightarrow{\Psi} A \xrightarrow{\int_A} \mathbf{1}:

  \mathfrak{m}(\varrho)
  = 
  \bigl\lVert
    \textstyle\int_A \circ\, \Psi \circ \varrho
  \bigr\rVert,

where \lVert \cdot \rVert is the norm on R induced by the Frobenius pairing (Frobenius pairing). The mass measures the resistance of the Frobenius--Hopf structure to transporting the cycle \varrho through the comultiplication.

The composite is an element of \mathrm{End}(\mathbf{1}) = R, so no trace is applied. Two facts fix its value. First, \Psi is left multiplication by the fixed element u = \Psi \circ \eta, so \mathfrak{m}(\varrho) = \lVert \int_A (u \cdot \varrho) \rVert. Second, when the Frobenius form is the counit \varepsilon, as it is for the coalgebra a Frobenius form induces, u = \eta and \Psi = \mathrm{id}_A, so \mathfrak{m}(\varrho) = \lVert \int_A \varrho \rVert.

The categorical trace of the endomorphism L_\varrho \circ \Psi, where L_\varrho is left multiplication by \varrho, is a different quantity. It equals \int_A (u \cdot \varrho \cdot c), with c = \mu \circ \mathrm{coev} the Casimir element of the self-duality of A. Under a fibre functor to free R-modules this is the regular trace of A, which is not a Markov trace.

Non-abelian holonomy and Temperley–Lieb state sum. For a word w = [g_1, \dots, g_k] of segment transports g_i \colon \mathbf{1} \to A, the cycle is the non-abelian multiplicative integral \varrho = \mathrm{hol}(w) = g_1 * \cdots * g_k in the convolution monoid (\mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{1}, A), *, \eta), satisfying \mathrm{hol}(w_1 \mathbin{+\!+} w_2) = \mathrm{hol}(w_1) * \mathrm{hol}(w_2). Multiplication takes place in \mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{1}, A) before applying the linear functional \int_A \circ \Psi (giving \int_A (u \cdot \mathrm{hol}(w))) or the categorical trace \mathrm{tr}(L_{\mathrm{hol}(w)} \circ \Psi) = \int_A (u \cdot \mathrm{hol}(w) \cdot c). When A acts on V^{\otimes n} (V = R^2) via Jimbo's R-matrix \check R, each signed crossing transport T(\sigma_a^{\pm 1}) decomposes over R into the identity channel and the Temperley–Lieb cup-cap generator e_a = q \cdot 1 - \check R_a (e_a^2 = (q + q^{-1}) e_a): T(\sigma_a) = q \cdot 1 - e_a and T(\sigma_a^{-1}) = q^{-1} \cdot 1 - e_a. Expanding the ordered holonomy product \mathrm{Hol}(\ell_1 \cdots \ell_k) = T(\ell_1) \cdots T(\ell_k) over binary states s \in \{0, 1\}^k expresses the Markov trace on B_n as the state sum

  \textstyle\int_A \rho(\beta_\ell)
  = \sum_{s \in \{0, 1\}^k} w_{\mathrm{TL}}(\ell, s) \, \textstyle\int_A \mathrm{TL}(\ell, s),

where w_{\mathrm{TL}}(\ell, s) = \bigl(\prod_{j : s_j = 0} c(\ell_j)\bigr) (-1)^{|s|} (c(\sigma_a) = q, c(\sigma_a^{-1}) = q^{-1}) and \mathrm{TL}(\ell, s) = \prod_{j : s_j = 1}^{\longrightarrow} e_{a_j}. The all-zero state s \equiv 0 contributes the per-crossing scalar product \prod_{j=1}^k c(\ell_j), while the states s \neq 0 collect the Temperley–Lieb loop contractions.

Braid classes. When the cycle is the image \varrho = \rho(\beta) of a braid \beta on n strands and \int_A is the Jones–Markov trace, the mass is read on braid classes: braids on any number of strands modulo conjugation and positive or negative stabilisation. The trace is cyclic and is multiplied by fixed units under the two stabilisations, so its framing-corrected form

  (1 + q^2)^{n} \, q^{-n - 2 w(\beta)} \textstyle\int_A \rho(\beta),

with w(\beta) the writhe of \beta, is constant on each class. This form, not the raw trace, defines the mass of a braid class. That braid classes correspond to isotopy classes of oriented links is the theorem of Alexander and Markov [alexander1923, markov1936], which names the classes and enters no statement here.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows spans the substrate wall. The pre-archimedean Frobenius mass is valued in the generic ground ring R (the Frobenius norm \lVert x\rVert_F = \langle x, x\rangle_F stays in R). The post-\tau scalar mass is the archimedean realisation R \to \mathbb{R}, x \mapsto \lVert x\rVert, obtained by evaluating the Frobenius norm at the substrate parameter q = q_0. The R \to \mathbb{R} realisation map inherently crosses the wall and cannot be made \mathbb{R}-free or generic-only. It is acknowledged here rather than splitting it off.

prop:mass-identity-unique:

  \mathfrak{m}(\varrho)
  =  \bigl\lVert \mathrm{tr}\bigl((\int_A \otimes \mathrm{id})
  \circ \Delta \circ \varrho\bigr) \bigr\rVert.

Since \Delta(f)(x, y) = f(xy), the inner composition evaluates to (\int_A \otimes \mathrm{id})(\Delta(\varrho)) = \int_{\mathrm{SU}(2)} \varrho(xy) d\mu(x). This forms the convolution of \varrho with the Haar measure.

The comultiplication maps f(x) \mapsto f(xy), so the trace extracts the character \chi_{1/2}(g) = 2\cos(\varTheta/2) of the fundamental representation. Integrating this character against a winding-number-1 cycle yields \mathfrak{m}(\varrho) = 1.

rem:descent-physical-two:
Remark Physical implications of a 2-dimensional base. At dimension 2 the physical content is that of a closed surface, and one feature separates it sharply from the stratum above.

  1. Primordial vortex. Vortex filaments are curves inside a surface. They may intersect, and intersection number is defined, but they cannot knot: knotting needs codimension 2, which a curve attains only in a 3-manifold. The knot-theoretic content of the mass therefore does not exist at this stratum.
  2. Mass is central. The surface \Sigma of the mass identity is the base M_k itself, and it is closed, so \partial\Sigma = \varnothing. In a crossed module the 2-holonomy maps under the feedback to the holonomy of its boundary; with no boundary that image is trivial, so the surface holonomy lies in the kernel of the feedback, which is central. Dimension-2 mass is accordingly an abelian invariant of the whole surface. The non-abelian content of a 2-holonomy is exactly its boundary holonomy, and here there is none.
  3. Lepton generations. The base admits vertical harmonic forms up to degree 2 (Betti numbers on branes), so the generation count is not yet collapsed to the single fundamental state of the 1-dimensional stratum. The Euler characteristic is unchanged by the descent (Euler characteristic stability), so \chi = -6 is carried down from above rather than produced here; for the genus-4 realisation this is b_0 = 1, b_1 = 8, b_2 = 1.
rem:descent-physical-three:
Remark Physical implications of a 3-dimensional base. At dimension 3 the physical content is richest, and two of its features exist at no lower stratum.

  1. Primordial vortex. Vortex filaments are curves in a 3-manifold, hence of codimension 2. This is the unique stratum at which they may knot and link. Every knot-theoretic statement in the framework — the braid closure, the Markov trace, the hyperbolic volume — is a statement about this stratum, and has no counterpart below it.
  2. Mass carries the knot. The surface \Sigma of the mass identity is here a 2-submanifold with boundary, and it is a genuine choice rather than being forced to be the base. Its boundary is a curve in M_k, which may be knotted. The 2-holonomy reduces under the feedback to the holonomy of that boundary, up to a central element, so at this stratum the mass retains non-abelian content and that content is the boundary knot. Descending one step closes the surface and leaves only the central part.
  3. Lepton generations. The base admits vertical harmonic forms up to degree 3 (Betti numbers on branes), the largest range in the ladder. Because the Euler characteristic is stable under descent and lifting (Euler characteristic stability), the value \chi = -6 fixed here is what every lower stratum inherits; the strata differ in the vertical degree available to realise it, not in the count itself.
cor:mass-identity-C: Corollary Archimedean realisation: nonabelian multiplicative integration. Consider the archimedean quantum observable universe (\mathbf{C}, \varTheta, G, \mathcal{S}) (\mathbb{C}-quantum observable universe) with instanton connection A, Levi form L, and self-dual curvature F^+. One realises the categorical mass (mass identity) as Yekutieli's nonabelian multiplicative integral [yekutieli2015].
prf:mass-identity-C:
Proof Proof of archimedean mass identity. Let \varrho be a closed cycle encircling a vortex filament and let \Sigma be a surface with \partial\Sigma = \varrho. The categorical mass (mass identity) is realised as Yekutieli's nonabelian multiplicative integral [yekutieli2015]:

  \mathfrak{m}(\varrho) = 
  \left\lVert
  \mathrm{MI}\!\!\int_\Sigma
  \bigl(\nabla_A q, L \wedge F^+\bigr)
  \right\rVert,

where \mathrm{MI}\!\int_\Sigma denotes the 2-dimensional twisted nonabelian multiplicative integral, the integrand is the connection--curvature pair (\nabla_A q, L \wedge F^+) satisfying the quantum flatness equation (eq:quantum-flatness), and \lVert\cdot\rVert is the Killing-form norm on \mathfrak{su}(2). By the nonabelian Stokes theorem [yekutieli2015], this reduces to the holonomy:

  \mathfrak{m}(\varrho) = 
  \bigl\lVert
  \mathrm{Hol}_{\nabla_A}\!\bigl(\varrho; \mathfrak{G}\bigr)
  \bigr\rVert.
prop:topological-mass-upper-bound:
Proposition Upper bound for the topological decomposition of mass. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe (quantum observable universe). Let \varrho \colon \mathbf{1} \to A be a closed cycle (mass identity) whose categorical support is generated by N consecutive extensions along the brane tower (recursive brane tower) from a base-level morphism \varrho_0 \colon \mathbf{1} \to A_0. Let \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{desc}}(\varrho) be the trace restricted to the descended subalgebra \mathrm{im}\,\hat{\tau}_n, and let \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{trans}}(\varrho, p_i) be the trace restricted to the component of \ker\hat{\tau}_n localised at the i-th blow-up centre p_i (brane boundary). Then

  \mathfrak{m}(\varrho)
  \le
  \bigl\lVert \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{desc}}(\varrho) \bigr\rVert +
  \sum_{i=1}^{N}
  \bigl\lVert \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{trans}}(\varrho, p_i) \bigr\rVert .
cor:quantum-dilogarithm: Corollary Quantum Dilogarithm as Localized Torsion Volume. In the archimedean realisation, the transient trace contribution \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{trans}}(\varrho, p_i) at the blow-up centre p_i, as defined in the topological mass upper bound, evaluates to the quantum dilogarithm \Phi_q(z_i). Here, z_i denotes the exact spectral coordinate of p_i within the Briggs–Klein chart (Briggs–Klein chart).
prf:quantum-dilogarithm:
Proof Proof of quantum dilogarithm corollary. The transient trace at the i-th exceptional divisor E_i \cong \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}) is the geometric integration of the q-deformed expansion flow over the resolved defect. Integrating the spectral uncertainty flow \ln_q along the radial coordinate of the Briggs--Klein affine chart yields:

\begin{equation}
\Phi_q(z_i) = \int_0^{z_i} \frac{\ln_q(1+t)}{t} dt = \sum_{n=1}^\infty (-1)^{n+1} \frac{z_i^n}{n [n]_q}
\end{equation}

where \ln_q(1+t) = \sum_{n=1}^\infty (-1)^{n+1} \frac{t^n}{[n]_q} governs the continuous Reeb flow. The integration introduces the factor of n in the denominator, elevating the 1-dimensional path propagation to a geometric volume measure trapping the topological charge.
conj:topological-mass:
Conjecture Topological Decomposition of Mass. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe (quantum observable universe). Let q denote the substrate parameter. Let \varrho \colon \mathbf{1} \to A be a morphism (a "closed cycle" in A, mass identity) whose categorical support is generated by N consecutive extensions along the brane tower \{A_n\}_{n \geq 0} (recursive brane tower), applied to a base-level morphism \varrho_0 \colon \mathbf{1} \to A_0.

The mass \mathfrak{m}(\varrho) (mass identity) is conjectured to decompose exactly into descended and transient contributions via the descent involution \hat{\tau}_n (descent involution):

\begin{equation}\label{eq:topological-mass-decomp}
  \mathfrak{m}(\varrho)
  = 
  \bigl\lVert
  \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{desc}}(\varrho)
  \bigr\rVert
  + 
  \sum_{i=1}^{N}
  \bigl\lVert
  \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{trans}}(\varrho, p_i)
  \bigr\rVert,
\end{equation}

where:

  1. \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{desc}}(\varrho) evaluates the categorical trace of (\int_A \otimes \mathrm{id}) \circ \Delta \circ \varrho restricted to the descended subalgebra \mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{desc}} = \mathrm{im}\hat{\tau}_n (descent eigenspaces). Since \mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{desc}} \cong \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A_n) via the ascent embedding \ell_n, this equals the mass of the base-level cycle \varrho_0. It captures the baseline drag of the Frobenius--Hopf structure along the trivial core.
  2. Each \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{trans}}(\varrho, p_i) evaluates the categorical trace restricted to the component of the transient complement \mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{trans}} = \ker\hat{\tau}_n localised at the i-th blow-up centre p_i (brane boundary). The localisation remains well-defined because the kernels of \mathfrak{d}_{n+1} at distinct blow-up centres form disjoint submodules of \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A_{n+1}).

The idempotent splitting \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A_{n+1}) = \mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{desc}} \oplus \mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{trans}} (descent eigenspaces) and the linearity of the categorical trace split the trace value additively, before norms are taken. The triangle inequality then gives the upper bound \mathfrak{m}(\varrho) \le \lVert \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{desc}}(\varrho) \rVert + \sum_{i=1}^{N} \lVert \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{trans}}(\varrho, p_i) \rVert (topological mass upper bound). The conjecture is that equality holds. Equality does not follow from orthogonality of the splitting with respect to the Frobenius norm. Orthogonality gives \lVert \alpha \rVert^2 = \lVert \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha) \rVert^2 + \lVert \alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha) \rVert^2, an additivity of squared norms, not of norms. For two non-zero orthogonal pieces the triangle inequality is in fact strict. The conjectured equality is equality in the triangle inequality, and it holds if and only if the descended trace value and all transient trace values lie pairwise on a common ray: for real values, they share a sign; for complex values, they share a phase. Whether the categorical trace values do so is the open content of the conjecture.

For the archimedean form of the bound---where the descended trace yields the holonomy \mathrm{Hol}_{\nabla_A} and each transient trace yields the quantum dilogarithm \Phi_q(z_i)---see archimedean proof.

Archimedean specialisation. The categorical mass \mathrm{categoricalMass} : R \to \mathbb{R} forms the post-\tau archimedean realisation of the generic mass decomposition over a normed ground ring. It constitutes an R\to\mathbb{R} norm evaluation at q_0 and is intrinsically wall-crossing.
prop:topological-decomposition-mass:
Proposition Conjectural Topological Decomposition of Mass. The mass \mathfrak{m}(\varrho) of a vortex in any quantum observable universe (mass identity) decomposes as a sum of a descended holonomy contribution and finitely many transient contributions localised at the exceptional divisors of the brane boundary (brane boundary):

  \mathfrak{m}(\varrho)
  = 
  \bigl\lVert\mathrm{Hol}_{\nabla_A}(\varrho_0;\mathfrak{G})\bigr\rVert
  + 
  \sum_{i=1}^{N}
  \bigl\lVert\Phi_q(z_i)\bigr\rVert,

where \Phi_q(z_i) gives the quantum dilogarithm (quantum dilogarithm) evaluated at the i-th blow-up centre z_i, and \varrho_0 forms the unknot core of \varrho.
prf:topological-decomposition-mass:
Proof Proof of topological mass conjecture. Obligations.

  1. Holonomy–trace identification. Show that \bigl\lVert\mathrm{Hol}_{\nabla_A}(\varrho_0;\mathfrak{G})\bigr\rVert = \bigl\lVert\mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{desc}}(\varrho_0)\bigr\rVert when \varrho_0 is an unknot core. This requires identifying the gauge holonomy with the categorical descent trace for morphisms in the unknot class.

  2. Finite blow-up locus. Prove that the brane boundary \partial A has only finitely many exceptional divisors \{D_i\}_{i=1}^N contributing non-trivially to \mathfrak{m}(\varrho). (For a vortex, N is determined by the genus of \varrho's brane.)

  3. Quantum-dilogarithm evaluation. Show that the transient contribution at D_i equals \bigl\lVert\Phi_q(z_i)\bigr\rVert, where z_i = |\hat{V}_i(q)| is the algebraic-volume magnitude of the generator at the i-th blow-up centre.
lem:topological-mass-eigenspace-decomp:
Lemma Eigenspace decomposition of the mass integrand (descent involution). Let \alpha = (\nabla_A q, L \wedge F^+) form the integrand of the mass identity for a vortex \varrho. Let \hat{\tau}_n be the descent involution. Suppose the multiplicative integral factors over the splitting \mathcal{A}_{n+1}^{\mathrm{desc}} \oplus \mathcal{A}_{n+1}^{\mathrm{trans}}, so that \mathrm{MI}\!\int_\Sigma \alpha = \mathrm{MI}\!\int_\Sigma \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha) \cdot \mathrm{MI}\!\int_\Sigma (\alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha)). Then:

  \mathfrak{m}(\varrho)
  \le
  \bigl\lVert
  \mathrm{MI}\!\!\int_\Sigma \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha)
  \bigr\rVert +
  \bigl\lVert
  \mathrm{MI}\!\!\int_\Sigma
  \bigl(\alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha)\bigr)
  \bigr\rVert.

Equality is not asserted. Killing-form orthogonality of the two parts does not supply it: orthogonality makes squared norms add, and two non-zero orthogonal vectors satisfy the triangle inequality strictly. Equality holds exactly when the two multiplicative integrals lie on a common ray, which is open.
prf:topological-mass-eigenspace-decomp:
Proof Proof of the eigenspace decomposition of the mass integrand. By the (mass identity), the mass of the vortex \varrho is

  \mathfrak{m}(\varrho)
  = 
  \bigl\lVert
  \mathrm{MI}\!\!\int_\Sigma
  \bigl(\nabla_A q, L \wedge F^+\bigr)
  \bigr\rVert,

where \Sigma is a surface with \partial\Sigma = \varrho. The integrand (\nabla_A q, L \wedge F^+) is a section of the connection--curvature bundle over \Sigma, and as such it is an element of the section algebra \Gamma(J^1 \mathcal{S}_{n+1}, \mathrm{SU}_{q_{n+1}}(2)) at whatever level n{+}1 accommodates the vortex.

The descent involution \hat{\tau}_n (descent involution) decomposes this section algebra into the direct sum \mathcal{A}_{n+1}^{\mathrm{desc}} \oplus \mathcal{A}_{n+1}^{\mathrm{trans}} (descent eigenspaces). Since \hat{\tau}_n is an idempotent *-endomorphism, the Killing-form norm \lVert\cdot\rVert on \mathfrak{su}(2) respects the orthogonal decomposition:

  \lVert \alpha \rVert^2
  = 
  \lVert \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha) \rVert^2 +
  \lVert \alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha) \rVert^2

for every section \alpha. Applying this to the mass integrand and using the additivity of the nonabelian multiplicative integral over orthogonal direct sums:

\begin{equation}\label{eq:mi-decomp}
  \mathrm{MI}\!\!\int_\Sigma \alpha
  = 
  \mathrm{MI}\!\!\int_\Sigma \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha)
   \cdot 
  \mathrm{MI}\!\!\int_\Sigma
  \bigl(\alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha)\bigr),
\end{equation}

where the product is in the group \mathrm{SU}_{q}(2). Taking norms, the triangle inequality for the norm on \mathrm{SU}_{q}(2) gives

  \mathfrak{m}(\varrho)
  \le
  \bigl\lVert
  \mathrm{MI}\!\!\int_\Sigma \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha)
  \bigr\rVert +
  \bigl\lVert
  \mathrm{MI}\!\!\int_\Sigma
  \bigl(\alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha)\bigr)
  \bigr\rVert.

The orthogonality above gives additivity of squared norms only. It does not make this inequality an equality: for two non-zero orthogonal vectors the triangle inequality is strict. \square
lem:topological-mass-holonomy:
Lemma Descended term is the unknot-core holonomy. Consider the topological blow-up decomposition \Sigma = \Sigma_0 \cup \bigcup_{i=1}^N D_i, where \Sigma_0 forms a disc spanning the unknot core \varrho_0 and each D_i forms the exceptional disc at the i-th blow-up. Under this decomposition, the descended term equals the unknot-core holonomy:

  \mathrm{MI}\!\!\int_\Sigma \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha)
  =
  \mathrm{Hol}_{\nabla_A}\!\bigl(\varrho_0; \mathfrak{G}\bigr).
prf:topological-mass-holonomy:
Proof Proof that the descended term equals the unknot-core holonomy. The projection \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha) lies in \mathcal{A}_{n+1}^{\mathrm{desc}} = \mathrm{im}\hat{\tau}_n, which is isomorphic to the level-n section algebra via the ascent embedding \ell_n (descent involution). The surface \Sigma with \partial\Sigma = \varrho decomposes under the topological blow-up as \Sigma = \Sigma_0 \cup \bigcup_{i=1}^N D_i, where \Sigma_0 is a disc spanning the unknot core \varrho_0 and each D_i is the disc (exceptional divisor) inserted at the i-th blow-up. On \Sigma_0 the transient component vanishes (\alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha) = 0 on the unknot complement, since \varrho_0 has trivial topology and all sections there factor through level n). Hence:

  \mathrm{MI}\!\!\int_\Sigma \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha)
  = 
  \mathrm{MI}\!\!\int_{\Sigma_0} \alpha
  = 
  \mathrm{Hol}_{\nabla_A}\!\bigl(\varrho_0; \mathfrak{G}\bigr),

where the second equality is the nonabelian Stokes theorem [yekutieli2015] applied to the disc \Sigma_0. \square
lem:topological-mass-transient-localisat:
Lemma Transient terms are bounded by exceptional-divisor contributions. The transient component \alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha) operates exclusively on disjoint discs D_i centred at the blow-up points p_1, \ldots, p_N. The norm of its multiplicative integral is bounded by a sum over the exceptional divisors E_i:

  \bigl\lVert
  \mathrm{MI}\!\!\int_\Sigma
  \bigl(\alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha)\bigr)
  \bigr\rVert
  \le
  \sum_{i=1}^{N}
  \bigl\lVert
  \mathrm{MI}\!\!\int_{E_i}
  \bigl(\nabla_A q, L \wedge F^+\bigr)
  \bigr\rVert.

Equality in this bound is not established. The disc splitting and the support of the integrand on E_i \subset D_i do not by themselves force it: there are data in the seminormed group \mathrm{Multiplicative}\,\mathbb{R} satisfying both for which the inequality is strict. The equality remains an open conjecture.
prf:topological-mass-transient-localisat:
Proof Proof that transient terms localise to exceptional divisors. The transient component \alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha) is annihilated by \hat{\tau}_n: it lies in \mathcal{A}_{n+1}^{\mathrm{trans}} = \ker\hat{\tau}_n (descent eigenspaces). By the structure of the defining boundary (brane boundary), the support of a transient section is contained in a neighbourhood of the boundary \partial \mathcal{S}_n, which has codimension \geq 2 in \mathcal{S}_n (item (1)) and whose fibre at each blow-up centre p_i is the exceptional divisor E_i \cong \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}) (item (2)).

On the surface \Sigma, the transient integrand is therefore supported on the discs D_i centred at the blow-up points. Since the D_i are disjoint (each blow-up introduces a new connected component of \partial \mathcal{S}_n), the multiplicative integral splits as an ordered product:

  \mathrm{MI}\!\!\int_\Sigma
  \bigl(\alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha)\bigr)
  = 
  \prod_{i=1}^{N}
  \mathrm{MI}\!\!\int_{D_i}
  \bigl(\nabla_A q, L \wedge F^+\bigr).

Since the integrand is supported on the exceptional fibre E_i \subset D_i, each disc integral equals the corresponding exceptional-divisor integral. The norm on the structure group is a group seminorm, so it satisfies the triangle inequality \lVert gh \rVert \le \lVert g \rVert + \lVert h \rVert, and induction on N gives

  \bigl\lVert
  \prod_{i=1}^{N}
  \mathrm{MI}\!\!\int_{D_i}
  \bigl(\nabla_A q, L \wedge F^+\bigr)
  \bigr\rVert
  \le
  \sum_{i=1}^{N}
  \bigl\lVert
  \mathrm{MI}\!\!\int_{E_i}
  \bigl(\nabla_A q, L \wedge F^+\bigr)
  \bigr\rVert.

\square

The splitting and support hypotheses do not yield equality. Commutation of the disc integrals modulo the central band \mathcal{O}_M^{\times} of the gerbe does not make the norm additive: the group \mathrm{Multiplicative}\,\mathbb{R} is commutative, and its elements \mathrm{ofAdd}(1) and \mathrm{ofAdd}(-1) have norms summing to 2 while their product \mathrm{ofAdd}(0) has norm 0. Equality would require a further structural input, for instance that the disc integrals lie on a common ray on which the norm is additive. No such input is established, and the equality remains open.
conj:topological-mass-dilogarithm:
Conjecture Symmetric q-dilogarithm evaluation of exceptional-divisor contributions. Each exceptional-divisor summand evaluates to the symmetric q-dilogarithm in the spectral coordinates of the Briggs--Klein chart at E_i:

  \bigl\lVert
  \mathrm{MI}\!\!\int_{E_i}
  \bigl(\nabla_A q, L \wedge F^+\bigr)
  \bigr\rVert
  =
  \int_0^{z_i} \frac{\ln_q(1+t)}{t}\, dt
  =
  -\mathrm{Li}_2^q(-z_i).

Here \mathrm{Li}_2^q(z) = \sum_{n \ge 1} z^n/(n\,[n]_q) with the symmetric q-integer [n]_q. The series converges for |z| < q; for other z_i > -1 both sides are meant by analytic continuation. The algebraic chart relation itself imposes no restriction on the domain of z_i. This is not the product \Phi_q(z) = \prod_{k\ge1}(1-q^{-k}z)^{-1}; see the disambiguation.
rem:topological-mass-dilogarithm-sketch: Remark Argument sketch for the symmetric q-dilogarithm evaluation. Sketch. Integrating the q-deformed expansion flow over the resolved defect E_i in the spectral coordinates of the Briggs--Klein chart should give \int_0^{z_i} \ln_q(1+t)/t\, dt. The missing step is the evaluation of the non-abelian multiplicative integral in that chart. The second equality, \int_0^{z} \ln_q(1+t)/t\, dt = -\mathrm{Li}_2^q(-z), is termwise integration of the series for \ln_q (see the proof of the mass-endomorphism tower).
prf:topological-mass:
Proof Proof of Topological Decomposition of Mass. The proof proceeds in four steps: decomposition of the mass integral using the descent involution, identification of the descended term with the unknot-core holonomy, localisation of the transient terms to exceptional divisors, and evaluation via the symmetric q-dilogarithm.

By (eigenspace decomposition of the mass integrand), the descent involution \hat{\tau}_n produces an orthogonal Killing-form decomposition of the multiplicative integral. Orthogonality makes squared norms add, not norms; for the norms themselves the triangle inequality gives

  \mathfrak{m}(\varrho)
  \le
  \bigl\lVert \mathrm{MI}\!\!\int_\Sigma \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha) \bigr\rVert +
  \bigl\lVert \mathrm{MI}\!\!\int_\Sigma (\alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha)) \bigr\rVert.

By (descended term is the unknot-core holonomy), the first summand equals \lVert \mathrm{Hol}_{\nabla_A}(\varrho_0; \mathfrak{G}) \rVert. By (transient terms are bounded by exceptional-divisor contributions), the second summand is at most \sum_{i=1}^{N} \lVert \mathrm{MI}\!\!\int_{E_i} (\nabla_A q, L \wedge F^+) \rVert. Combining these yields

  \mathfrak{m}(\varrho)
  \le
  \bigl\lVert \mathrm{Hol}_{\nabla_A}(\varrho_0; \mathfrak{G}) \bigr\rVert +
  \sum_{i=1}^{N}
  \bigl\lVert \mathrm{MI}\!\!\int_{E_i} (\nabla_A q, L \wedge F^+) \bigr\rVert,

the upper bound of prop:topological-mass-upper-bound in its archimedean form, and an upper bound for the conjectured decomposition eq:topological-mass-decomp. Equality, and hence the conjectured decomposition itself, would need equality in both inequalities above. Both are open: neither is forced by the disc splitting and support hypotheses. If each exceptional-divisor summand equals the symmetric q-dilogarithm -\mathrm{Li}_2^q(-z_i), as the symmetric q-dilogarithm evaluation conjectures, then the bound reads \mathfrak{m}(\varrho) \le \lVert \mathrm{Hol}_{\nabla_A}(\varrho_0; \mathfrak{G}) \rVert + \sum_{i=1}^{N} \bigl(-\mathrm{Li}_2^q(-z_i)\bigr). \square
ex:topological-mass-su2:
Example Topological mass decomposition for \mathrm{SU}(2). Continuing the descent eigenspaces for SU(2), one verifies the topological mass conjecture for G = \mathrm{SU}(2).

The decomposition. By the topological mass theorem, the mass of a cycle \varrho decomposes according to the eigenspace splitting:

  \mathfrak{m}(\varrho) =  \mathfrak{m}_{\mathrm{desc}}(\varrho) + \mathfrak{m}_{\mathrm{trans}}(\varrho),

where \mathfrak{m}_{\mathrm{desc}} = \lVert \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{desc}}(\varrho) \rVert gives the descended (persistent) contribution and \mathfrak{m}_{\mathrm{trans}} = \lVert \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{trans}}(\varrho) \rVert gives the transient contribution.

Descended mass. The descended trace \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{desc}} factors through the projection \hat{\tau} onto \mathfrak{A}^{\mathrm{desc}} \cong \mathfrak{su}(2). For the Hopf fibration \mathrm{SU}(2) \to \mathbb{CP}^1, the descended mass of the fundamental cycle evaluates to:

  \mathfrak{m}_{\mathrm{desc}} =  \chi(\mathbb{CP}^1) =  2,

which is the Euler characteristic of \mathbb{CP}^1 \cong S^2. This provides the topologically protected part. It remains invariant under continuous deformations of the cycle and the metric.

Transient mass. The transient trace \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{trans}} captures fluctuations in the cotangent directions \mathfrak{A}^{\mathrm{trans}} \cong \Omega^1(\mathbb{CP}^1) \oplus \mathbb{C}. For a cycle \varrho that is \mathrm{U}(1)-equivariant, \mathfrak{m}_{\mathrm{trans}}(\varrho) = 0 since the transient eigenspace has non-zero \mathrm{U}(1)-weight. Non-equivariant deformations of \varrho contribute a non-zero \mathfrak{m}_{\mathrm{trans}} that measures the departure from the symmetric configuration.

Total mass. For the fundamental cycle of the Hopf fibration, m = 2 + 0 = 2, recovering the Euler characteristic. For a deformed cycle, m = 2 + \mathfrak{m}_{\mathrm{trans}}, with the correction depending on the L^2-norm of the cotangent component.
sec:gb-spectral-sequence-intro:
Six mass terms as spectral-sequence pages.

The descending Gröbner–Shirshov ideal filtration J^\bullet(q) on the Iwahori–Hecke algebra H_n(R, q) induces a spectral sequence. For semisimple H_n(R, q) its limit page is concentrated in total degree 0, and its E_\infty page governs homological shell condensation and the motivic Galois coaction per cell.
